kbd.$description: Keyboard key cap. Component tokens reference semantic tokens; a literal here is a decision this component owns, and the description is why.

corner.$description: The ramp, capped so a 20px key cap stays legibly square.

font-size.$description: Key labels are interface micro-copy: the micro role, set in Qeet UI. Small enough to sit inside a menu row or a button without crowding the label beside it.

foreground.$description: Secondary rather than tertiary text: a key label is 11px, so it takes the stronger of the two quiet text roles (7:1 or better on every surface in both themes) and stays restrained through size and the cap, not through low contrast.

background.$description: A translucent tint of the cap's own text colour, not a fixed surface. Key hints sit on canvases, cards, menus, command palettes and buttons; a tint lifts the cap off whichever of them it is on, in both themes, and follows a consumer who recolours the text (an inverse tooltip) without a second override.

border.$description: The cap outline, derived from the text colour for the same reason as the background. Decorative: the label carries the information, so it does not need 3:1.

elevation.$description: A one-pixel lower lip that doubles the bottom edge, so the cap reads as a key rather than a chip. Same tint as the border, restated rather than referenced so the shadow does not alias a colour token. Inset, so it never changes the cap's box; forced-colours mode strips it and the border remains.
